what_happened: Found an explicit L-plus marker gadget (theta := not-m AND allFuture m pins the evaluation point exactly; nu := theta OR F theta marks the closed past) that lets the open-future modal's existential dual express a gap-anchored past property Delta-prime that U/S cannot reach. This converts route R3a from 'find a bisimulation' into a concrete, compiled computation plus a GHR-12.4.2-style collapse argument over Q-time.

Discovered mid-round that the frame-constraint Limit blocks the naive 'permissive Q-frame' the negative construction needed: at a frame whose states are the atom colours alone, distinct states must be unrelated at all small durations, so over a dense duration a finitely-many-states history is a uniformly-discrete step function with no accumulating run structure. Resolved by routing through the repository's own colourClock (Semantics/Frames/TranslationProduct.lean), whose clock component discharges Limit while leaving the colour component free; colourFibre + its IsRegular instance compile. A second, smaller cost: the colourClock wrapper's internal Nonempty instance blocks ofReflectiveRegular_taskRel from unifying, so the 'every colour function is a history' step stayed a one-line audited paper step instead of compiling.

The companion task's plan (specs/854_.../plans/01_open-future-elimination-module.md) is a near-exact structural template for this task: same directory genre, same five-surface gate set (scoped build, C14 heredoc pair, theorem-index rows, generated inventories, full audit). Decomposition was calibrated against it rather than derived from scratch, and its measured phase timings supplied the effort estimates.

The task description asserts 'This will be the first Metalogic-to-OpenLanguage import in the library -- legal, but new'. That is no longer true: the companion elimination module FormalSystem/Metalogic/Expressiveness/OpenFutureElimination.lean already imports FormalSystem.OpenLanguage and landed first. The layering conclusion (downward edge, allowlist unchanged) is unaffected, but the novelty framing is stale and the plan states the current fact instead.

Description deliverable (2) 'a module row in FormalSystem/Metalogic/Independence/README.md, matching that file's existing row shape' understates the surface. That README's Modules table is a GENERATED inventory block (BEGIN GENERATED: inventory dir=...), so the row is produced by --emit-inventory, not hand-written. The hand-authored surfaces a new module actually obliges are: the 'Thirteen results are carried here' numbered list and its count sentence, duplicated verbatim in FormalSystem/Metalogic/Independence.lean's module docstring; the Key Results bullet list; the Dependencies 'Imports from' bullet; and two Last verified dates. Additionally the new module changes typst/generated/status.typ's file and line counts, gated by typst-sync-check.sh Check 2, and FormalSystem.lean, gated by C33 -- neither named in the description's scope list. Plan covers all of them.

Territory overlap with concurrent sibling task 559, which declares docs/theorem-index.md and FormalSystem/Metalogic.lean in its file_scope and (as a new-module task) will also regenerate FormalSystem.lean, typst/generated/status.typ and FormalSystem/Metalogic/README.md's generated inventory blocks. Four shared paths, none of them declared by the sibling for three of the four. Plan records the collision in Risks and requires a re-read immediately before each edit plus explicit-file-list staging in every phase that touches a shared path.
